newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton ends barely lower, focus on spread.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton ends barely lower, focus on spread.

text.p: NYCE May cotton futures settled lower as the floor remained focused on the May/July spread, trading sources said.
Speculators continued to roll short May positions into July. The May/July spread grew to a 1.70 premium in July from 1.66 on Wednesday's close.

The spot month finished 0.13 cent lower at 70.75 cents a lb after trading from 71.35 to 70.60 cents, slightly above the contract low hit Wednesday. July went out 0.09 weaker at 72.45 cents, while the outer months finished 0.06 to 0.30 weaker.
Volume was estimated at 15,000 lots compared with Wednesday's official 25,710 lots.
First notice day for the May contract is April 24.

USDA export and sales report put exports for the week ended April 10 at 180,200 bales. The figure was 28 percent below the previous week's marketing year high and 11 percent below the four-week average, USDA said.
The U.S. posted new sales of 95,800 bales for the current crop. Total commitments rose to 6.235 million bales. USDA has forecast exports of 7.0 million bales for the season.
Certificated stocks remained unchanged from the previous session but still high at 221,862 bales, as of Wednesday.
Open interest in May fell 3,686 lots to 20,544 lots as of Tuesday's close. Open interest in July climbed 2,980 lots to 28,935 lots.
